title: The Sublime Object: Ljubljana, the Cause freudienne, and the Philosopher on Camera
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Coast and the Faculty of Arts

stops.name: Ljubljana, the birth of an economist's son
stops.date_confidence: attested; day, month and year all fixed by the standard biography. The birth clinic is not: a pool entry naming the Ljubljana University Medical Centre carried a coordinate 800 m off the hospital and conceded the venue was a proxy, so the city coordinate is used instead.
stops.campa: Slavoj Žižek is born in Ljubljana on the twenty-first of March, 1949, in a republic four years into its socialist experiment and one year into its break with Moscow. His father Jože is an economist and civil servant, his mother Vesna an accountant; the household is secular, salaried and comfortable, the sort the new state is building on purpose. The life that follows will be narrated obsessively by the man living it, but the opening is thin. No published biography names the clinic. No plaque marks any building. The record fixes a city and a day.
suggested_refs: Ljubljana civil register for March 1949; no birth-clinic record has been produced by any published biography
sources: Rex Butler, Slavoj Žižek: Live Theory (2005), biographical chapter, cited at second hand

stops.name: Portorož, the coast that got the films first
stops.date_confidence: decade only; sources place part of his childhood in Portorož without naming a year. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The family keeps time on the Adriatic, in the resort town of Portorož on the Slovene sliver of coast an hour from Trieste. Italian radio carries across the water, western films reach the cinemas, and the shop windows hold goods most of Yugoslavia will not see for another decade. A boy raised here meets capitalism as spectacle years before he meets it as theory, and his books will keep that order. The sources place part of his childhood on this coast and give no year for any of it, only that the coast came before the capital.
suggested_refs: Portorož in the 1950s as Yugoslavia's western shop window, one hour from the Italian border

stops.name: Ljubljana, the Bežigrad classroom
stops.date_confidence: inferred from age; sources give only the school, not the years of attendance. Month and day defaulted to 01, and the school's own campus coordinate was not verified, so the city pin stands.
stops.campa: Back in Ljubljana the boy is enrolled at Bežigrad High School, in the district north of the river where the socialist republic puts its stadium and its new apartment blocks. The curriculum is the standard Yugoslav one, Marxism included and examinable. He is already reading past it. The school gets one line in every later account, and in the decades of interviews he returns instead to the films and the paperbacks that came across a border his passport could cross.
suggested_refs: Gimnazija Bežigrad, Ljubljana, and the standard Yugoslav secondary curriculum of the early 1960s

stops.name: Ljubljana, Aškerčeva 2: the first Derrida in Slovene
stops.date_confidence: year attested for both the enrolment and the Derrida translation; month and day defaulted to 01. Coordinate corrected: a pool entry gave 46.0479 / 14.4983, about 300 m northwest of the Aškerčeva 2 address.
stops.campa: At eighteen he enters the Faculty of Arts on Aškerčeva cesta to read philosophy and sociology. The faculty is the entire intellectual apparatus of a small nation housed in one building, and it will throw him out before it pays him. In the same year he publishes the first Slovenian translation of a text by Jacques Derrida, which is to say that a first-year student in Ljubljana is importing Paris in real time, ahead of most of the English-speaking world. The translation appears in 1967, the earliest in any Yugoslav language.
suggested_refs: Filozofska fakulteta, Aškerčeva cesta 2, Ljubljana
The 1967 Slovenian Derrida translation, the earliest in any Yugoslav language

stops.name: Ljubljana, the journals a federation allows itself
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the sources give a span across the late 1960s and 1970s with no dated first appearance. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He writes for the journals a socialist federation permits itself as a pressure valve: Praxis, and in Ljubljana Tribuna and Problemi. The register runs Heideggerian, then structuralist, then Lacanian; the politics stay heterodox enough to be noticed and formal enough to be defensible. Around these pages a circle forms that will later be called the Ljubljana school, with Mladen Dolar, Renata Salecl and Alenka Zupančič. For the moment it is a handful of graduate students arguing in a language spoken by two million people.
suggested_refs: Problemi and Tribuna, Ljubljana, and the Praxis school's journal
The Ljubljana school of psychoanalysis in its Slovene-language phase, before any English translation

stops.name: Ljubljana, the thesis found non-Marxist
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day defaulted to 01. A pool entry described 1971 as an undergraduate degree with a thesis on French structuralism, which conflates it with the 1981 doctorate; the 1971 event is the dismissal following the Master's thesis.
stops.campa: His Master's thesis is read by the authorities and found non-Marxist, and the assistant researcher post he holds at the university is taken from him. The verdict is not a philosophical one. In a state whose legitimacy rests on one reading of Marx, a young man importing Lacan and Heidegger and Derrida into the seminar is an administrative problem, solved administratively. He is twenty-two years old. What follows the decision is four years of military service and unemployment.
suggested_refs: University of Ljubljana personnel decisions of 1971 concerning the assistant researcher post

stops.name: Karlovac, the garrison on the Kupa
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the sources name Karlovac and a four-year span of service and unemployment, but no induction date, discharge date or unit. Year chosen as the midpoint, month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Somewhere inside the four years every biography compresses into a phrase, he is conscripted into the Yugoslav People's Army. No source in reach gives the unit, the induction date, or the day he was let out. The army is the one institution that puts every republic of the federation in a single room under a single language of command, and he will spend a career explaining how ideology holds a state together after its slogans have stopped convincing anyone. He meets the mechanism first at Karlovac, a Habsburg star fortress on the Kupa kept under Tito as a barracks town.
suggested_refs: The Yugoslav People's Army as the federation's last all-republic institution
The Karlovac star fortress, Habsburg military frontier

stops.name: Ljubljana, the translator's workshop
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the translation and editing work is attested across the 1970s and 1980s without dated individual volumes in reach. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Barred from teaching, he works as a translator, and the work becomes the apparatus. Jacques Lacan into Slovene, Sigmund Freud into Slovene, Louis Althusser into Slovene: a small language acquires a psychoanalytic vocabulary because one unemployed philosopher builds it word by word. The editions come out across the 1970s and 1980s, and no source in reach dates the individual volumes. The books he writes later are audible here as a stack of other men's sentences. Translation is the slowest possible reading, and nothing else would have driven him through the Ecrits at that pace.
suggested_refs: Slovene editions of Lacan, Freud and Althusser edited and translated by Žižek in the 1970s and 1980s

stops.name: Ljubljana, the Institute for Sociology and Philosophy
stops.date_confidence: the post is attested and dated in the pool from 1979; month and day defaulted to 01. A pool entry naming the Institute of Philosophy of ZRC SAZU at Novi trg 2 is a different body and is not followed here.
stops.campa: The University of Ljubljana takes him back, not into a lecture hall but into the Institute for Sociology and Philosophy as a senior researcher: a post with no students and no obligation to be orthodox in front of anyone. Eight years earlier the same university took a post away from him for holding the views it now pays him to hold in private. He keeps this one for the rest of his working life. Every visiting chair and every semester away, in New York or London or Saas-Fee, is taken from this base and returned to it. The employer never changes.
suggested_refs: Institute for Sociology and Philosophy, University of Ljubljana, the standing appointment behind every visiting post

stops.name: Ljubljana, the doctorate on French structuralism
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the Doctor of Arts; month and day defaulted to 01. The dissertation title, The Theoretical and Practical Relevance of French Structuralism, was misassigned by one pool entry to a 1971 undergraduate degree.
stops.campa: He defends a Doctor of Arts in philosophy at the University of Ljubljana, on the theoretical and practical relevance of French structuralism, ten years after the same institution found his thesis insufficiently Marxist. Nothing in his position has moved; the work that cost him a job in 1971 earns him the degree in 1981, from the same faculty, on the same subject. What has moved is the state around it. Yugoslavia is one year past Tito, the economy sliding, the ideological policing distracted by larger failures.
suggested_refs: The Theoretical and Practical Relevance of French Structuralism, University of Ljubljana dissertation, 1981

stops.name: Saint-Denis, the university that May 1968 built
stops.date_confidence: contested; a pool entry dated his Paris VIII period 1978-1985 and asserted contact with the old Vincennes site before its 1980 demolition, which nothing in reach supports. The early 1980s are the conventional dating. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He goes to Paris, to the university that May 1968 built: Paris VIII, moved out of Vincennes to a concrete campus at Saint-Denis after the bulldozers took the old site down over three days in August 1980. Here he registers under Jacques-Alain Miller. The department is the one Michel Foucault staffed at its founding and where Gilles Deleuze taught his entire career, two men he will later spend whole books arguing against. Whether he ever saw the Vincennes site before the bulldozers is not established by anything in reach.
suggested_refs: Université Paris VIII Vincennes-Saint-Denis, 2 rue de la Liberté, Saint-Denis
The demolition of the Vincennes campus, 27-29 August 1980
sources: gilles_deleuze.journey.json (stops on the Vincennes department and seminar)
michel_foucault.journey.json (stop on the Vincennes philosophy department)

stops.name: Paris, la Cause freudienne
stops.date_confidence: attested for the institutional context; Lacan dies 9 September 1981 and the École de la Cause freudienne was founded by Miller in 1980-81. Day defaulted to 01. Pin inherited unchanged from jacques_lacan.journey.json.
stops.campa: Jacques Lacan dies in September 1981, having dissolved his own school the year before and left the succession to his son-in-law. What remains is the École de la Cause freudienne, Miller's institution, and it is here rather than in any room where Lacan himself spoke that Žižek is formed. He receives the master through the executor: the transcripts Miller edits, the doctrine Miller polices, the circle Miller convenes. No source claims the two men ever met, and the window in which they could have was a matter of months.
stops.quote: As a Marxist, let me add: if anyone tells you Lacan is difficult, this is class propaganda by the enemy.
stops.quote_source: Žižek, closing remark in an interview for the CN8 programme Nitebeat, 2003
suggested_refs: École de la Cause freudienne, founded by Jacques-Alain Miller after the dissolution of the École freudienne de Paris
sources: jacques_lacan.journey.json (stop 'Paris: la Cause freudienne', 1980-02-21, pin inherited here)

stops.name: Paris, the couch and the seminar circuit
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the analysis and training inside Miller's circle are attested in outline but undated, and the rue Huysmans address is the modern premises used as a landmark proxy. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He undergoes analysis inside Miller's circle and moves through the seminar rooms of the Cause freudienne on the Left Bank. Which rooms, and in which years, no source in reach records. He takes the material the way it is transmitted there, as a practice with a couch attached rather than only a literature. The graph of desire that Lacan drew across Seminar V at Sainte-Anne, and presented at Royaumont in 1960 under the title of the subversion of the subject, is handed to him as working equipment. He will carry it out of France and bolt it onto a theory of ideology.
suggested_refs: Lacan's Seminar V at the amphithéâtre Magnan, Hôpital Sainte-Anne, 1957-58, where the graph of desire is first drawn
'Subversion of the Subject and the Dialectic of Desire', Abbaye de Royaumont, 19 September 1960
sources: jacques_lacan.journey.json (stops on Seminar V at Sainte-Anne and the Royaumont colloquium, cited as the source of the material, not as stops of this traveler)

stops.name: Saint-Denis, the second doctorate defended
stops.date_confidence: contested: two pool lenses and Wikipedia give 1986, a third gives 1985. Followed as 1986, disagreement recorded rather than resolved. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He defends a second doctorate, in psychoanalysis, under the title La philosophie entre le symptôme et le fantasme. He is thirty-seven and holds two of them, one from a socialist republic and one from the school Lacan's heir runs. What he has actually built in Paris is a machine: Hegelian dialectic driven by Lacanian categories, capable of taking any object at all, a film, a joke, a lavatory, a constitution, and returning the structure of desire lodged inside it. Three years from now he will point it at ideology. Sources give the defence as 1986; one gives 1985.
stops.quote: Lacan's definition of human deception: We deceive the Other by means of the truth itself
stops.quote_source: The Sublime Object of Ideology (Verso, 1989), p. 41, written three years after the defence
suggested_refs: La philosophie entre le symptôme et le fantasme, Université Paris VIII dissertation, supervised by Jacques-Alain Miller

segments.name: 1988: The Party Card and the Book

stops.name: Colchester, Wivenhoe Park: Laclau reads the Slovene
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the Essex connection is drawn from Laclau's interviews and Žižek's acknowledgments, with no dated meeting or correspondence in reach. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: At the University of Essex, on the parkland campus outside Colchester, Ernesto Laclau has built a school of discourse theory out of Gramsci and post-Marxism, and he reads the Slovene. No dated meeting and no correspondence survives in reach; the connection is drawn from Laclau's interviews and from Žižek's own acknowledgments. Without an Argentine at an English new university with an appetite for Lacanian Marxism, the Ljubljana school stays in Slovene for another decade. Laclau edits the manuscript, routes it toward Verso, and writes the preface telling English readers who this is.
suggested_refs: Ernesto Laclau's preface to The Sublime Object of Ideology
The Essex school of discourse theory, University of Essex, Wivenhoe Park
sources: Ernesto Laclau's interviews on the Essex school, cited at second hand

stops.name: Ljubljana, the trial of the four and the resignation
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested for the resignation from the League of Communists of Slovenia; day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Four men are tried by a military court in Ljubljana for revealing an army document, and the proceedings are conducted in Serbo-Croatian in the capital of a republic that speaks Slovene. Tens of thousands stand outside the courtroom. The JBTZ trial fuses a scattered civil society into a movement, and the state that once found his thesis insufficiently Marxist now has three years left to run. In October, at thirty-nine, Žižek gives up the party card and resigns from the League of Communists of Slovenia.
suggested_refs: The JBTZ trial, Ljubljana military court, 1988, and the crowds outside it

stops.name: Ljubljana, Pogled s strani
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day defaulted to 01. The title is glossed as both 'A Glance Askew' and 'A Glance Sideways' in different sources; neither rendering is adjudicated.
stops.campa: His first book on film theory appears in Slovene as Pogled s strani, a look taken from the side, the angle at which an object gives up the shape it hides when faced head on. Hitchcock is already the workhorse. The readership numbers in the low thousands, in a language with no market past the republic's borders. Twelve months later the same method in English will carry his name out of the republic, and this book will be listed thereafter as a curiosity of the bibliography. Sources gloss the title as both A Glance Askew and A Glance Sideways, and neither rendering has been settled.
suggested_refs: Pogled s strani, Ljubljana, 1988, Žižek's first book on film

stops.name: Ljubljana, the Committee for the Defence of Human Rights
stops.date_confidence: the activism is attested for 1988-1990 without dated individual actions; the year is chosen as the midpoint and month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He is on the committees. The Committee for the Defence of Human Rights, grown directly out of the trial of the four, is where Slovene civil society organises itself between 1988 and 1990: petitions, rallies, the drafting of demands that would have been sedition a year earlier. Žižek works inside the committee, a philosopher among lawyers and journalists and rock critics, doing the ordinary business of an opposition that does not yet know it is going to win, and no source in reach dates a single one of his appearances. The federal constitution is read aloud in public against the army that wrote it.
suggested_refs: Odbor za varstvo človekovih pravic, Ljubljana, 1988-1990

stops.name: London, Meard Street: The Sublime Object of Ideology
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested for publication; day defaulted to 01. The Soho address is a Verso address historically associated with the house, not a verified 1989 office.
stops.campa: Verso publishes The Sublime Object of Ideology, and a forty-year-old researcher from a republic most English readers cannot find on a map becomes, inside a season, the most cited living theorist of ideology. The argument is that ideology does not work by fooling anybody. People know exactly what they are doing and go on doing it, because the doing is held in place by an enjoyment that knowing cannot touch. Hegel, Marx, Lacan and Althusser are rebuilt into a single apparatus and handed over in English.
stops.quote: The cynical subject is quite aware of the distance between the ideological mask and the social reality, but he none the less still insists upon the mask
stops.quote_source: The Sublime Object of Ideology (Verso, 1989), p. 29
suggested_refs: The Sublime Object of Ideology, Verso, London, 1989
The Ljubljana school of psychoanalysis, whose method this book carried into Anglophone theory
sources: English Wikipedia, 'The Sublime Object of Ideology'
Wikiquote transcription of the 1989 Verso text, p. 29

stops.name: Ljubljana, fifth of twelve
stops.date_confidence: attested; first round of the 1990 Slovenian presidential election, 8 April 1990. A pool entry staging the campaign at Cankarjev dom is dropped, its own note having conceded the venue was unconfirmed.
stops.campa: Slovenia holds its first multi-party elections: four seats on a collective state presidency, twelve candidates on the ballot. Žižek stands for the Liberal Democratic Party and takes 9.68 percent of the vote, fifth of the twelve, one place outside the presidency of a country that is about to declare itself. The philosopher of ideology comes within a few thousand ballots of governing. He never runs again, and in every later telling it is a joke he is glad to repeat. The first round is held on 8 April 1990.
suggested_refs: 1990 Slovenian presidential election, first round, 8 April 1990: twelve candidates for four seats

stops.name: Ljubljana, Trg republike: independence declared
stops.date_confidence: attested for the declaration of independence at Trg republike; Žižek's presence in the crowd is inferred from his residence and public role, not from a named record.
stops.campa: On Republic Square, beneath the two concrete slabs Edvard Ravnikar set beside the parliament, Slovenia declares itself independent of Yugoslavia. Žižek is in the city and not on the platform: he missed the seat by one place fifteen months before, and the state he would have helped govern is born without him inside it. Ten days of war follow, then the federation begins coming apart in earnest further south, and he will spend the next decade explaining the wreck to audiences who do not live in it. Whether he stood in the square that evening is not recorded anywhere in reach.
suggested_refs: Trg republike, Ljubljana, and Edvard Ravnikar's twin towers
The Ten-Day War, 27 June to 7 July 1991
sources: General historical record of the Slovenian declaration of independence, 26 June 1991

stops.name: Cambridge, Massachusetts: Looking Awry
stops.date_confidence: year attested for publication by MIT Press; month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: MIT Press publishes Looking Awry: An Introduction to Jacques Lacan through Popular Culture, and the template is set for the next thirty years. Hitchcock, film noir, detective fiction and science fiction are not illustrations of Lacan in this book; they are the places where Lacan's categories can be caught working in public. A theory that in French was defended by initiation is now available to a graduate student who has seen Vertigo. Academic Lacanianism in English dates from here more than from any translation. The subtitle says introduction, and the press means it.
suggested_refs: Looking Awry: An Introduction to Jacques Lacan through Popular Culture, MIT Press, 1991

stops.name: Ann Arbor, the lecture circuit opens
stops.date_confidence: decade only; the Michigan visiting appointments are attested as a 1990s-2000s pattern with no dated term in reach. Year chosen as representative, month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He begins the life of the circuit: a visiting appointment at Michigan, a hall filled past capacity, a talk delivered without notes at a speed the room struggles to follow, then an airport. No source in reach dates a single one of the Michigan terms. American universities in the nineties are buying continental theory by the seminar, and he arrives with Hegel, Lacan and Hitchcock inside the same forty minutes. The journalists start calling him the Elvis of cultural theory.
suggested_refs: University of Michigan visiting appointments, cited in Žižek profile pieces
sources: University visiting-scholar records cited at second hand in profile journalism

stops.name: Vienna, the Institute for Human Sciences
stops.date_confidence: decade only; the IWM fellowship is attested as a 1990s-2000s affiliation with no dated term. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The Institute for Human Sciences on the Spittelauer Lände takes him as a visiting fellow. Vienna after 1989 is the hinge the whole region turns on, a city built to look east, and the institute exists to bring the thought of the former socialist countries into a conversation that had ignored it for forty years. He works out of Sigmund Freud's categories in an idiom Freud would not have recognised, a mile up the canal from the consulting room at Berggasse 19 where the private practice opened in 1886.
suggested_refs: Institut für die Wissenschaften vom Menschen, Spittelauer Lände 3, Vienna
Freud's practice at Berggasse 19, opened 25 April 1886, cited here as the source of the categories, not as a stop of this traveler

stops.name: New York, the New School in the winter after
stops.date_confidence: decade only for the New School lecturing; the year is chosen to match the composition and publication of Welcome to the Desert of the Real (Verso, 2002). Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He lectures at the New School on West 12th Street, the institution New York founded for exiles, in the winter after the towers came down. Welcome to the Desert of the Real is written in these months: an argument that the attack was received in America as a film America had already made about itself many times over, and that the shock was the shock of the fantasy arriving in the real. He does not soften it for a room full of people who watched the thing from their own windows. Verso publishes the book in 2002.
stops.quote: We feel free because we lack the very language to articulate our unfreedom.
stops.quote_source: Welcome to the Desert of the Real! (Verso, 2002), p. 2
suggested_refs: Welcome to the Desert of the Real!, Verso, 2002
The New School for Social Research, 66 West 12th Street, New York
sources: Wikiquote transcription of Welcome to the Desert of the Real!, p. 2

stops.name: Saas-Fee, Hegel at altitude
stops.date_confidence: decade only; the European Graduate School professorship is attested for the 2000s without dated terms. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Each summer the European Graduate School convenes at Saas-Fee, a car-free village under the Mischabel glaciers, and a faculty of continental theorists teaches media and communication for a fortnight. Žižek is on the roster with the rest of them. Students climb to a valley with no road in and receive Hegel at five thousand feet, in terms no source in reach has dated. Whether the arrangement is a serious institution or a summer camp for theory depends on who is asked.
suggested_refs: European Graduate School, Saas-Fee, Valais, summer seminars in media and communication

stops.name: New York, the Abercrombie & Fitch catalog
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He writes the accompanying essay for a quarterly catalog of the clothing retailer Abercrombie & Fitch, set beside Bruce Weber's photographs of near-naked American teenagers. The critique of ideology accepts a commission from the object of the critique, and is paid for it. His critics date the swallowing of the philosopher by the performance from here. His defence, offered often and in the same words, is that refusing to touch the commercial machine is the gesture that leaves it standing, and that the academy's purity is itself a very comfortable ideology.
suggested_refs: The Abercrombie & Fitch Quarterly, 2003, with photographs by Bruce Weber and an essay by Žižek

stops.name: New York University, Global Distinguished Professor
stops.date_confidence: decade only; the NYU title is attested as a recurring appointment spanning the 2000s to the 2020s, with no start date in reach. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He holds the title Global Distinguished Professor of German at New York University, one of the standing American appointments he cycles through without ever giving up Ljubljana. New York is also where the case against him is argued loudest: that the output has outrun the thinking, and that a man who publishes fifty books cannot still be reading. Tony Judt, dying in Manhattan and asked about the future of the public intellectual, gives the sentence that gets quoted back at him longest.
stops.quote: If he is the future of public intellectuals, then they have no future.
stops.quote_source: Tony Judt, 'the last interview', 2010, speaking about Žižek
suggested_refs: NYU Global Distinguished Professorship in German
Tony Judt's last interview, 2010
sources: Judt interview text, retrieved via secondary transcription

stops.name: Berlin, Liebe Dein Symptom wie Dich selbst
stops.date_confidence: year attested. Place contested: Wikipedia calls the film a German documentary, while the pool's place field read 'Germany/Austria' and carried a Vienna coordinate. A German coordinate is used and the disagreement recorded; treat the pin as country-level at best.
stops.campa: A German television documentary appears under the title Liebe Dein Symptom wie Dich selbst, love thy symptom as thyself, and the format that will carry him to a mass audience is found: put the philosopher on camera, let him talk at speed, cut the theory against the images it is about. Sources disagree on where it was made, one calling it German and another Germany and Austria. He is forty-seven and still unknown outside the seminar rooms. Every film made about him afterwards works the same way, because he films well and the tics survive editing.
suggested_refs: Liebe Dein Symptom wie Dich selbst!, German television documentary, 1996

stops.name: Toronto, the festival premiere of Žižek!
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested for the Toronto International Film Festival premiere; day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Astra Taylor's Žižek! premieres at the Toronto International Film Festival, a feature documentary following him through lecture halls, airports and his own apartment. From this festival onward there are two Žižeks, the one who is read and the one who is watched, and the second is by an order of magnitude the larger. The camera finds what the books cannot show: the sniffing, the tugging at the shirt front, the hands, the accent, the jokes delivered faster than the subtitles can carry them.
suggested_refs: Žižek!, dir. Astra Taylor, 2005, TIFF premiere

stops.name: London, the recreated sets of The Pervert's Guide to Cinema
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the film; the filming location is a gap. No studio or set-build site is publicly documented, and the London coordinate is an admitted placeholder. The film is a UK, Austrian and Netherlands co-production.
stops.campa: Sophie Fiennes builds him sets. No studio or set-build site is publicly documented for any of it. He delivers the commentary on The Birds from inside a replica of the rowing boat on Bodega Bay, and on the rest from reconstructions of the rooms the films were shot in, so that the critic stands physically inside the picture he is reading and the theory arrives as a scene instead of a lecture. It runs two and a half hours, and it is the best known thing he has ever made and the least like a book.
stops.quote: My relationship towards tulips is inherently Lynchian... flowers should be forbidden to children.
stops.quote_source: The Pervert's Guide to Cinema, dir. Sophie Fiennes, 2006; the retrieved transcription carries an internal ellipsis and may compress two separate remarks
suggested_refs: The Pervert's Guide to Cinema, dir. Sophie Fiennes, 2006, UK/Austria/Netherlands co-production
sources: Sophie Fiennes, production notes for The Pervert's Guide to Cinema

stops.name: London, The Pervert's Guide to Ideology
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the film; filming location unconfirmed, London coordinate used as an admitted placeholder.
stops.campa: Six years on, Fiennes and Žižek run the method again, aimed this time not at cinema but at ideology, with the films kept as evidence: They Live and its sunglasses, Titanic and its class arrangement, The Sound of Music and its singing nuns. The argument is that ideology is not the coat thrown over the system but the thing the system runs on. Partway through, he is sitting in a rubbish dump among the refuse of consumption, delivering the commentary from inside it.
stops.quote: I already am eating from the trash can all the time. The name of this trash can is ideology
stops.quote_source: Žižek, spoken on screen in The Pervert's Guide to Ideology, dir. Sophie Fiennes, 2012
suggested_refs: The Pervert's Guide to Ideology, dir. Sophie Fiennes, 2012

stops.name: Zuccotti Park, the human microphone
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the speech is transcribed and widely reprinted.
stops.campa: He comes to the occupied plaza in lower Manhattan and speaks through the human microphone, every phrase repeated back by the crowd because amplification is banned in the park. What he brings is not encouragement. The danger, he tells them, is that the occupation becomes a memory its participants are fond of, a good time had in a square, and that the system absorbs the carnival and alters nothing. The crowd repeats the warning against itself, clause by clause, and then cheers it. The speech is transcribed on the day and has been reprinted many times since.
stops.quote: Don't fall in love with yourselves. We have a nice time here. But remember, carnivals come cheap.
stops.quote_source: Žižek, address to Occupy Wall Street, Zuccotti Park, 9 October 2011, transcript published by Verso and n+1
suggested_refs: Zuccotti Park, Lower Manhattan, and the Occupy Wall Street encampment, autumn 2011

stops.name: Ljubljana, the square in winter
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; Žižek is named among prominent supporters of the 2012-2013 Slovenian protests, but no dated appearance and no venue is confirmed in accessible sources. Month chosen at the start of the protest wave, day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Slovenia's winter of protest fills the same square where independence was declared twenty-one years before: austerity, a banking collapse, a mayor and a prime minister accused of assets they never declared. Which day he spoke, and where, no accessible source records. The republic he came within one place of helping to govern is having its first crisis of legitimacy as a capitalist democracy. Žižek speaks for the demonstrators, in Slovene, to a country of two million where he is a household figure rather than a theorist to be introduced.
suggested_refs: The 2012-2013 Slovenian uprisings, Trg republike and Ljubljana city centre

stops.name: Athens, the summer of the referendum
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; his public support for the Greek left in 2015 is reported, but no venue and no dated appearance is confirmed. The central Athens coordinate is a placeholder and the month is chosen for the referendum.
stops.campa: Greece votes on the terms of its own bankruptcy, and Žižek is in Athens for it, standing with Syriza and with Yanis Varoufakis in the weeks when a small indebted country tests whether a referendum can outrank a creditor. No source in reach names a venue or a day for his appearance. He has argued for years that the European left's real problem is that it does not want power, only the moral position of opposing power. Athens in July 2015 is the test case, and the left is offered capitulation or exit and takes neither cleanly.
stops.quote: I'm not certain that people who are reading Zizek are actually drawn very much nearer rethinking the problems of the left.
stops.quote_source: Eric Hobsbawm, published conversation on Marx and the New Left, 2011; retrieved through a secondary transcription, not a primary transcript

stops.name: Berlin, the Volksbühne: DiEM25 launched
stops.date_confidence: attested; DiEM25 was launched at the Volksbühne am Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz on 9 February 2016, and Žižek is a documented member from 2016. This dated anchor upgrades a Volksbühne entry the pool had left as an undated recurring pattern.
stops.campa: In the Volksbühne on Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz, the East Berlin theatre that kept a left repertoire through the socialist state and through whatever replaced it, Yanis Varoufakis launches DiEM25, a movement to democratise the European Union before it comes apart. Žižek joins. After a quarter of a century of commentary he attaches himself to an actual organisation, with a programme, a membership and a deadline written into its name. The launch is held on 9 February 2016.

stops.name: Knightsbridge, the embassy conversation
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the exchange is reported for 2016 without a fixed date, and sources disagree on whether Žižek was physically inside the embassy or joined by video link. The contradiction is recorded, not resolved. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Julian Assange has been inside the Ecuadorian embassy on Hans Crescent for four years, unable to step onto a Knightsbridge pavement without arrest. Žižek and Varoufakis take part in a publicised conversation with him on WikiLeaks, on transparency, and on what a state is entitled to keep back from the people it governs. Whether Žižek was in the building or on a screen is reported both ways and is not settled here. The one door is watched around the clock by the Metropolitan Police, at a cost the newspapers itemise every few months.

stops.name: Bloomsbury, Birkbeck: the international directorship
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the start of the Birkbeck Institute directorship; month and day defaulted to 01. Two pool entries dated it 'c. 2001' and '1990s', both impossible: the Institute did not exist before 2004.
stops.campa: Birkbeck, the University of London college that teaches in the evenings to people who work through the day, opens its Institute for the Humanities in 2004 and makes him international director. He holds the post twenty-one years, longer than he holds any other appointment except the Ljubljana research post he was given in 1979. What it gives him is a London room, a budget for conferences, and an audience of adults who came to Malet Street after a shift somewhere else.

stops.name: Ljubljana, the fourth marriage
stops.date_confidence: the marriage to Jela Krečič is attested as his fourth and is widely reported for 2013, though the Wikipedia Personal life section does not date it. No wedding venue is named in any source in reach; Ljubljana stands as his home base, not as an attested venue.
stops.campa: He marries Jela Krečič, a Slovene journalist, author and philosopher, his fourth wife. The third marriage, to the Argentinian model Analía Hounie, is over. Two adult sons, Tim and Kostja, come from earlier in the sequence and are named in the record without further comment. For a man who has built a career on the gap between what people say they want and what they actually do, the private life is documented in one short paragraph and defended in none of the fifty books. No source in reach names a wedding venue, for this marriage or any of the others.

stops.name: Chicago, Critical Inquiry and the borrowed pages
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested for the Newsweek report; day defaulted to 01. A pool entry describing the affair as concerning 'Hegel and the film Antigone's Claim' with a defence of careless notes is wrong on every element and is not followed.
stops.campa: Bloggers find that an article of his in Critical Inquiry reproduces passages from Stanley Hornbeck's review of Kevin MacDonald, published in a white-nationalist magazine, and Newsweek prints the finding in July. Separately the New York Times accuses him of reusing his own earlier pages in an op-ed. His explanation is that a friend supplied him the material and told him it could be used freely, and he apologises for not knowing that his friend's summary was itself borrowed. At fifty books, the machinery shows through. He does not slow down.

stops.name: London, the RT studio
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the start of the programme; month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He begins hosting How to Watch the News with Slavoj Žižek for RT, the television network funded by the Russian state, and the objection is immediate and obvious: the philosopher of ideology has taken a chair inside a propaganda operation in order to explain from it how propaganda works. He treats the objection as evidence for his standing thesis about liberal purity, and nothing in reach records the channel objecting to anything he has said on it. The channel pays him and airs him. The programme runs from 2019.

stops.name: Toronto, Meridian Hall: the debate of the century
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the venue is the former Sony Centre for the Performing Arts, 1 Front Street East, renamed Meridian Hall.
stops.campa: Three thousand people fill the old Sony Centre on Front Street and thousands more pay to watch the stream: Žižek against Jordan Peterson on whether happiness is better served by capitalism or by Marxism. It is billed as the debate of the century. What the audience gets is two men who have not read each other closely, agreeing at length in front of a crowd that bought tickets for a fight. It is the most watched philosophical event of the decade and settles nothing at all. The hall has since been renamed Meridian Hall.
stops.quote: Žižek is an extreme example of it. I don't see anything to what he's saying.
stops.quote_source: Noam Chomsky, remarks in a 'Virtual Town Hall' interview, 2012, speaking about Žižek

stops.name: London, the directorship ends
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested for the end of the Birkbeck Institute directorship; day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: In September 2025 the Birkbeck appointment ends, twenty-one years after it began. He is seventy-six. The Ljubljana research post he was given in 1979 he still holds, the books still arrive faster than any reviewer can keep pace with, and the lecture clips circulate to an audience that has never opened one of them and never will. Fifty-four years earlier a committee in this same profession decided he was insufficiently Marxist and took his job away. He is still writing.
